questions.text:
निम्नलिखित घटनाओं को कालक्रम अनुसार व्यवस्थित कीजिए और उत्तर के रूप में सही विकल्प चुनिए :
(i) भारत-रूस सामरिक संधि
(ii) अफगानिस्तान पर सोवियत आक्रमण
(iii) सोवियत संघ का विघटन
(iv) रूस में समाजवादी क्रांति
questions.text_english:
Arrange the following events in chronological order and choose the correct option as answer:
(i) Indo-Russian Strategic Agreement
(ii) The Soviet invasion of Afghanistan
(iii) Disintegration of the Soviet Union
(iv) Socialist Revolution in Russia
questions.solution: The correct chronological order is Option C: (iv), (ii), (iii), (i). The Socialist Revolution in Russia occurred in 1917, establishing the Soviet state. The Soviet invasion of Afghanistan took place in 1979. The disintegration of the Soviet Union happened in 1991. The Indo-Russian Strategic Agreement was signed in 2000. Options A, B, and D place these events out of their correct historical sequence.
questions.solution_hindi: सही कालक्रम विकल्प C है: (iv), (ii), (iii), (i)। रूस में समाजवादी क्रांति 1917 में हुई। अफगानिस्तान पर सोवियत आक्रमण 1979 में हुआ। सोवियत संघ का विघटन 1991 में हुआ। भारत-रूस सामरिक संधि 2000 में हस्ताक्षरित हुई।
questions.topic: Soviet Union and Cold War Chronology

questions.text: स्वतंत्रता के ठीक पश्चात् भारत के नियोजित विकास के लिए निम्नलिखित में से किसका गठन किया गया था ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following was formed for the planned development of India, just after independence ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is Option B: Planning Commission. The Planning Commission was established in 1950, shortly after independence, to oversee planned economic development in India through Five-Year Plans. The Election Commission handles elections, not development planning. The Shah Commission was formed much later to investigate the Emergency period. NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission only in 2015.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर विकल्प B है: योजना आयोग। 1950 में स्वतंत्रता के तुरंत बाद योजना आयोग की स्थापना पंचवर्षीय योजनाओं के माध्यम से नियोजित आर्थिक विकास की देखरेख के लिए की गई थी।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से भारत की कौन सी एक देसी रियासत ने शुरुआत में भारतीय संघ में शामिल होने का विरोध किया था ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following Princely States of India initially opposed joining the Indian Union ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is Option B: Hyderabad. The Nizam of Hyderabad initially refused to join the Indian Union and wanted to remain independent or join Pakistan. Sardar Patel had to use police action (Operation Polo) in September 1948 to integrate Hyderabad into India. Baroda, Mysore, and Gwalior did not resist joining India in the same manner.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर विकल्प B है: हैदराबाद। हैदराबाद के निजाम ने शुरू में भारतीय संघ में शामिल होने से इनकार कर दिया था। सरदार पटेल को सितंबर 1948 में ऑपरेशन पोलो के माध्यम से सैन्य कार्रवाई करनी पड़ी।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन नवीकरणीय ऊर्जा के उपयोग को प्रोत्साहित करता है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following encourages the use of renewable energy ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is Option A: Energy Conservation Act. The Energy Conservation Act (2001) in India specifically promotes the efficient use of energy and encourages the adoption of renewable energy sources. The Environment Protection Act focuses on pollution control. The Electricity Act deals with the regulation of the power sector broadly. The National Auto Fuel Policy addresses vehicle emissions standards, not renewable energy promotion specifically.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर विकल्प A है: ऊर्जा संरक्षण अधिनियम। ऊर्जा संरक्षण अधिनियम (2001) विशेष रूप से ऊर्जा के कुशल उपयोग और नवीकरणीय ऊर्जा को प्रोत्साहित करता है।

सूची-I का सूची-II से सही मिलान कीजिए :

questions.text_english:
Match the List-I with the List-II correctly :
List-I:
(a) The first country to liberalise its economy in the South Asian region.
(b) Earlier this country had the Sultan as its Head of State. Now, it is a republic.
(c) A land locked country.
(d) In the conflict between the military and the pro-democracy groups, the military had prevailed over democracy in this country.
List-II:
(i) Maldives
(ii) India
(iii) Pakistan
(iv) Nepal
questions.solution: The correct answer is Option C: (a)-(ii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(iii). India (ii) was the first in South Asia to liberalise its economy in 1991. Maldives (i) was formerly a Sultanate and became a republic in 1968. Nepal (iv) is a landlocked country surrounded on all sides by land. Pakistan (iii) has witnessed repeated military dominance over civilian democracy, with multiple military coups in its history.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर विकल्प C है। भारत ने 1991 में दक्षिण एशिया में सबसे पहले अपनी अर्थव्यवस्था का उदारीकरण किया। मालदीव पहले सल्तनत था और 1968 में गणराज्य बना। नेपाल एक स्थलरुद्ध देश है। पाकिस्तान में बार-बार सेना का शासन रहा है।
questions.topic: South Asian Countries - Political and Economic Features

questions.text:
नीचे दिए गए प्रश्न में दो कथनों को क्रमशः अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) के रूप में अंकित किया गया है। उत्तर के रूप में सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए।
अभिकथन (A) : भारत में चौथे आम चुनाव से पहले, लोगों ने आवश्यक वस्तुओं की कीमतों में वृद्धि, खाद्यान्नों की कमी तथा बढ़ती हुई बेरोजगारी के विरुद्ध आन्दोलन शुरू कर दिए।
कारण (R) : मानसून की असफलता, व्यापक सूखा, खेती की पैदावार में गिरावट तथा गंभीर खाद्य संकट ने समस्या पैदा की।
questions.text_english:
In the following question, a statement of Assertion (A) is followed by a statement of Reason (R). Choose the correct option as answer.
Assertion (A): People started protesting against the increase in prices of essential commodities, food scarcity and growing unemployment before the fourth General elections in India.
Reason (R): Failure of monsoons, widespread drought, decline in agricultural production and serious food shortage caused the problem.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, लेकिन कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, लेकिन कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both the Assertion (A) and the Reason (R) are correct and the Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both the Assertion (A) and the Reason (R) are correct, but the Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: The Assertion (A) is correct, but the Reason (R) is incorrect.
options_english.D: The Assertion (A) is incorrect, but the Reason (R) is correct.

questions.solution: The correct answer is Option A. Both the Assertion and the Reason are correct, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. Before the fourth general elections in India (1967), there were widespread protests against rising prices, food scarcity and unemployment. This situation was directly caused by the failure of monsoons, widespread drought in 1965-66, a sharp decline in agricultural output, and a severe food crisis — which is exactly what Reason (R) states. Thus R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर विकल्प A है। अभिकथन और कारण दोनों सही हैं और कारण, अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या करता है। 1967 के चौथे आम चुनाव से पहले मानसून की असफलता, सूखे और खाद्य संकट के कारण जनआंदोलन हुए।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा विकासशील देश जनसंख्या की वृद्धि दर को सफलतापूर्वक नियंत्रित करने वाला पहला देश था ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following developing countries was the first to successfully control the rate of growth of population ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is Option A: India. India was the first developing country in the world to officially adopt a national family planning programme in 1952, making it a pioneer in efforts to control population growth. Pakistan, Nepal, and Sri Lanka adopted similar policies much later. India's early and sustained family planning initiatives made it the first developing nation to attempt systematic population control.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर विकल्प A है: भारत। भारत 1952 में राष्ट्रीय परिवार नियोजन कार्यक्रम अपनाने वाला विश्व का पहला विकासशील देश था।

questions.text: भारत के योजना आयोग के स्थान पर नीति आयोग का गठन किया गया क्योंकि _______
questions.text_english: Planning Commission of India was replaced with NITI Aayog because _______

options.A: यह बहुत पुराना हो गया था।
options.B: यह विकास की नई चुनौतियों का सामना करने में अप्रासंगिक होता जा रहा था।
options.C: यह पूरी तरह से समाजवादी मॉडल पर आधारित था।
options.D: कई राज्य योजना आयोग के पक्ष में नहीं थे।

options_english.B: it was becoming irrelevant to face the new challenges of development.
options_english.C: it was totally based on Socialist model.
options_english.D: many states were not in favour of Planning Commission.

questions.solution: The correct answer is Option B. The Planning Commission was replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015 because it was becoming increasingly irrelevant in addressing the new challenges of development in a liberalised and globalised economy. The Planning Commission was designed for a centrally planned, socialist-style economy and could not effectively adapt to cooperative federalism and the dynamic market-oriented development needs of 21st century India. Option A is incorrect as age alone was not the reason. Option C is partially true but not the primary stated reason. Option D is not accurate.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर विकल्प B है। 2015 में योजना आयोग को नीति आयोग से इसलिए बदला गया क्योंकि यह उदारीकृत और वैश्वीकृत अर्थव्यवस्था में विकास की नई चुनौतियों का सामना करने में अप्रासंगिक होता जा रहा था।

questions.text: लाल बहादुर शास्त्री की मृत्यु के बाद, प्रधानमंत्री पद के लिए इंदिरा गांधी और निम्नलिखित में से किस एक के बीच तीव्र प्रतिस्पर्धा थी ?
questions.text_english: After the death of Lal Bahadur Shastri, there was an intense competition for the post of Prime Minister between Indira Gandhi and which one of the following ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is Option A: Morarji Desai. After the sudden death of Lal Bahadur Shastri in 1966, there was a fierce contest for the Prime Minister's post within the Congress party between Indira Gandhi and Morarji Desai. The Congress President K. Kamraj and the Syndicate (group of powerful Congress leaders) backed Indira Gandhi, who ultimately won. Morarji Desai was the main rival in this leadership contest.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर विकल्प A है: मोरारजी देसाई। 1966 में लाल बहादुर शास्त्री की मृत्यु के बाद, कांग्रेस में इंदिरा गांधी और मोरारजी देसाई के बीच प्रधानमंत्री पद के लिए तीव्र प्रतिस्पर्धा हुई।

questions.text:
नीचे दिए गए प्रश्न में दो कथनों को क्रमशः अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) के रूप में अंकित किया गया है। उत्तर के रूप में सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए।
अभिकथन (A) : वर्तमान में वैश्विक वातावरण गर्म होता जा रहा है।
कारण (R) : धरती के समताप मण्डल में ओज़ोन गैस की मात्रा में लगातार कमी हो रही है।
questions.text_english:
In the following question, a statement of Assertion (A) is followed by a statement of Reason (R). Choose the correct option as answer.
Assertion (A): Presently the global atmosphere is warming up.
Reason (R): A steady decline in the total amount of Ozone in the earth's stratosphere.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, लेकिन कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, लेकिन कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both the Assertion (A) and the Reason (R) are correct, and the Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both the Assertion (A) and the Reason (R) are correct, but the Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: The Assertion (A) is correct, but the Reason (R) is incorrect.
options_english.D: The Assertion (A) is incorrect, but the Reason (R) is correct.

questions.solution: The correct answer is Option B. Both the Assertion and the Reason are correct, but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion. Global warming (A) is primarily caused by the greenhouse effect — the accumulation of carbon dioxide, methane and other greenhouse gases in the atmosphere. Ozone depletion (R) is also a real and factually correct phenomenon, but it is primarily responsible for increased UV radiation reaching the Earth's surface, not for global warming per se. Since both statements are true but R does not correctly explain A, Option B is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर विकल्प B है। अभिकथन और कारण दोनों सही हैं, लेकिन कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है। वैश्विक ताप वृद्धि का कारण ग्रीनहाउस गैसें हैं, जबकि ओज़ोन क्षरण UV विकिरण से संबंधित है।

questions.text: किस घटना ने सोवियत संघ में साम्यवाद के अंत को चिन्हित किया ?
questions.text_english: Which event marked the end of Communism in the Soviet Union ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is Option C: Disintegration of the Soviet Union. The disintegration of the Soviet Union in December 1991 marked the definitive end of Communist rule in the USSR, as it led to the dissolution of the world's first communist state into 15 independent republics. The Cuban Missile Crisis (1962) was a Cold War confrontation but did not end communism. The New World Order emerged as a consequence, not a cause. The rise of the US economy was a separate development.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर विकल्प C है: सोवियत संघ का विघटन। दिसंबर 1991 में सोवियत संघ के विघटन ने USSR में साम्यवादी शासन के अंत को चिन्हित किया।

questions.text: उस राज्य का नाम लिखिए जिसमें से छत्तीसगढ़ को बनाया गया था।
questions.text_english: Name the state from which Chhattisgarh was carved out.
questions.solution: The correct answer is Option D: Madhya Pradesh. Chhattisgarh was carved out of the southeastern part of Madhya Pradesh on 1 November 2000. It became the 26th state of India. At the same time, Uttarakhand was carved from Uttar Pradesh, and Jharkhand from Bihar. Jharkhand itself is a state, not the origin of Chhattisgarh.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर विकल्प D है: मध्य प्रदेश। छत्तीसगढ़ को 1 नवंबर 2000 को मध्य प्रदेश के दक्षिण-पूर्वी भाग से अलग करके बनाया गया था।

questions.text: जून 1992 में रियो-डी-जेनेरियो में आयोजित 'पृथ्वी शिखर-सम्मेलन' के किन्हीं दो परिणामों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Explain any two outcomes of the 'Earth Summit' held in June 1992 at Rio-de-Janeiro.

key_points: The Earth Summit produced Agenda 21, a comprehensive blueprint for sustainable development.
It led to the signing of the Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) to combat global warming.
The Convention on Biological Diversity was also opened for signature.
The concept of Common But Differentiated Responsibilities was established.

questions.solution: The Earth Summit held in Rio de Janeiro in June 1992 had two major outcomes. First, it produced Agenda 21, a comprehensive action plan for sustainable development that addressed environmental protection, social equity, and economic development at global, national, and local levels. Second, the Summit led to the signing of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), which committed member states to reduce greenhouse gas emissions to address global warming. Additionally, it established the principle of Common But Differentiated Responsibilities, recognizing that developed nations bore greater responsibility for environmental degradation and must lead in providing solutions.
questions.solution_hindi: जून 1992 में रियो-डी-जेनेरियो में आयोजित पृथ्वी शिखर-सम्मेलन के दो प्रमुख परिणाम रहे। प्रथम, इसमें एजेंडा-21 तैयार किया गया जो सतत विकास के लिए एक व्यापक कार्य योजना थी। द्वितीय, जलवायु परिवर्तन पर संयुक्त राष्ट्र फ्रेमवर्क कन्वेंशन (UNFCCC) पर हस्ताक्षर हुए, जिसने वैश्विक ताप को नियंत्रित करने की प्रतिबद्धता जताई। इसके अलावा 'समान किंतु विभेदित जिम्मेदारियों' के सिद्धांत को भी मान्यता मिली।

questions.text: पर्यावरण और प्राकृतिक संसाधनों के मुद्दे, विश्व राजनीति का हिस्सा क्यों बन गए हैं ? किन्हीं दो कारणों का विश्लेषण कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Analyse any two reasons as to why issues of environment and natural resources have become a part of the World Politics.

key_points: Environmental degradation and resource depletion affect all nations, creating shared global concerns.
Competition over scarce natural resources like oil and water leads to geopolitical conflicts.
Climate change impacts are cross-border in nature, requiring international cooperation.
Economic development models of nations directly impact global environmental health.

questions.solution: Environmental and natural resource issues have become central to world politics for two key reasons. First, environmental challenges such as climate change, ozone depletion, and loss of biodiversity are transboundary in nature — they cannot be contained within national borders and affect all countries regardless of their level of development. This has forced nations to engage in international negotiations and agreements. Second, natural resources like oil, water, and fertile land are finite and increasingly scarce. The competition among nations to secure access to these resources has led to geopolitical rivalries, conflicts, and the formation of strategic alliances, making resource security a core component of international relations and foreign policy.
questions.solution_hindi: पर्यावरण और प्राकृतिक संसाधनों के मुद्दे दो प्रमुख कारणों से विश्व राजनीति का हिस्सा बन गए हैं। प्रथम, जलवायु परिवर्तन, ओज़ोन क्षरण जैसी पर्यावरणीय समस्याएँ सीमाओं से परे जाती हैं और सभी देशों को प्रभावित करती हैं, जिससे अंतरराष्ट्रीय सहयोग आवश्यक हो जाता है। द्वितीय, तेल, जल और उपजाऊ भूमि जैसे प्राकृतिक संसाधन सीमित हैं और इन पर नियंत्रण के लिए देशों के बीच भू-राजनीतिक प्रतिस्पर्धा होती है।

questions.text: 1992 में संयुक्त राष्ट्र महासभा द्वारा पारित प्रस्ताव में सम्मिलित संयुक्त राष्ट्र सुरक्षा परिषद् से संबंधित किन्हीं दो शिकायतों को स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Explain any two complaints related to the U.N. Security Council reflected in the resolution passed by the U.N. General Assembly in 1992.

key_points: The Security Council composition does not reflect the contemporary world order as it still reflects 1945 power structures.
The veto power of the five permanent members is undemocratic and allows powerful nations to block decisions.
Developing and smaller nations have inadequate representation.
The Council is dominated by Western powers and does not represent Asia, Africa, or Latin America adequately.

questions.solution: The 1992 UN General Assembly resolution highlighted two main complaints about the Security Council. First, the composition of the Security Council was considered outdated as it still reflected the power structure of 1945, when only five countries were given permanent membership with veto power. The world had changed significantly with decolonisation and the emergence of many new independent nations, yet these countries had no permanent representation. Second, the veto power enjoyed by the P5 was seen as deeply undemocratic, as any one of the five permanent members could block a resolution even if the rest of the world supported it, making the Council an instrument of great power politics rather than collective security.
questions.solution_hindi: 1992 के UNGA प्रस्ताव में सुरक्षा परिषद के संबंध में दो प्रमुख शिकायतें थीं। प्रथम, सुरक्षा परिषद की संरचना पुरानी पड़ गई है क्योंकि यह 1945 की शक्ति-संरचना को दर्शाती है जो समकालीन विश्व का प्रतिनिधित्व नहीं करती। द्वितीय, पाँच स्थायी सदस्यों का वीटो अधिकार अलोकतांत्रिक है, जो एक महाशक्ति को पूरी दुनिया की इच्छा के विरुद्ध किसी प्रस्ताव को रोकने की शक्ति देता है।

questions.text: भारत के राजनीतिक और चुनावी इतिहास में वर्ष 1967 को एक महत्वपूर्ण पड़ाव मानने के कोई दो कारण स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Explain any two reasons to consider the year 1967 as a landmark year in India's political and electoral history.

key_points: The Congress party lost its dominant position in many states, ending the one-party dominance.
Several non-Congress coalition governments came to power in various states for the first time.
The phenomenon of defections (Aaya Ram Gaya Ram) began, changing the nature of Indian politics.
The 1967 elections showed the growing political assertiveness of regional parties and voters.

questions.solution: The year 1967 is considered a landmark in India's political and electoral history for two significant reasons. First, it marked the end of the Congress party's era of dominance, as the party suffered major defeats in many states. Congress lost power in eight states, and several non-Congress coalition governments came to power in states like Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, and Punjab for the first time. Second, the 1967 elections witnessed the phenomenon of large-scale political defections — famously captured by the phrase 'Aaya Ram Gaya Ram' — where elected legislators switched parties frequently, introducing instability and signalling the fragmentation of Indian politics that would characterise the coming decades.
questions.solution_hindi: 1967 भारत के राजनीतिक और चुनावी इतिहास में दो कारणों से एक महत्वपूर्ण पड़ाव है। प्रथम, कांग्रेस की एकदलीय प्रभुता का अंत हुआ क्योंकि पार्टी आठ राज्यों में सत्ता से बाहर हो गई और कई राज्यों में पहली बार गैर-कांग्रेसी सरकारें बनीं। द्वितीय, 'आया राम गया राम' की राजनीतिक दल-बदल की घटना सामने आई, जिसने भारतीय राजनीति की प्रकृति को बदल दिया।

questions.text: राजीव गांधी और हरचंद सिंह लोंगोवाल द्वारा 1985 में हस्ताक्षरित पंजाब समझौते के किन्हीं दो प्रावधानों का उल्लेख कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Mention any two provisions of the Punjab Accord signed by Rajiv Gandhi and Harchand Singh Longowal in 1985.

key_points: Chandigarh was to be transferred to Punjab.
A Commission (Mathew Commission) was to be set up to resolve the river water dispute between Punjab and Haryana.
A separate commission was to be appointed to look into the territorial disputes between Punjab and Haryana.
Fresh elections were to be held in Punjab.

questions.solution: The Punjab Accord of 1985, also known as the Rajiv-Longowal Accord, contained two important provisions. First, it was agreed that Chandigarh, which was serving as the joint capital of both Punjab and Haryana, would be transferred to Punjab as its exclusive capital. Second, a Commission (the Mathew Commission) was to be constituted to examine and resolve the long-standing river water sharing dispute between Punjab, Haryana, and Rajasthan concerning the Ravi-Beas river waters. Additionally, a separate Commission was to demarcate the territories between Punjab and Haryana. The accord aimed to address Sikh grievances and restore peace in Punjab.
questions.solution_hindi: 1985 में हस्ताक्षरित पंजाब समझौते के दो प्रमुख प्रावधान थे। प्रथम, चंडीगढ़ को पंजाब को सौंपने का निर्णय लिया गया। द्वितीय, पंजाब, हरियाणा और राजस्थान के बीच रावी-ब्यास नदी के जल-बंटवारे के विवाद को सुलझाने के लिए एक आयोग (मैथ्यू आयोग) गठित करने का प्रावधान किया गया।

questions.text: गठबन्धन की सरकारों के कोई दो लाभ स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Explain any two advantages of Coalition governments.

key_points: Coalition governments represent diverse groups and communities, making governance more inclusive.
They reflect the multi-party nature of Indian democracy and provide a platform for regional parties.
They prevent the excessive concentration of power in one party.
They promote consensus-based decision making.

questions.solution: Coalition governments offer two significant advantages. First, they ensure broader representation of diverse communities, regions, and ideological groups in the government. In a diverse country like India, coalition governments allow regional parties and smaller groups to participate in governance, making policies more sensitive to the varied needs of different parts of the country. Second, coalition governments act as a check against the concentration of power in a single party. Since multiple parties share power, important decisions are taken through negotiation and consensus, promoting democratic accountability and preventing authoritarian tendencies that might arise when one party has an overwhelming majority.
questions.solution_hindi: गठबन्धन सरकारों के दो प्रमुख लाभ हैं। प्रथम, ये सरकारें विविध समुदायों, क्षेत्रों और विचारधाराओं का व्यापक प्रतिनिधित्व सुनिश्चित करती हैं तथा क्षेत्रीय दलों को शासन में भागीदारी का अवसर देती हैं। द्वितीय, ये सत्ता के केंद्रीकरण को रोकती हैं क्योंकि महत्वपूर्ण निर्णय सहमति से लिए जाते हैं, जिससे लोकतांत्रिक जवाबदेही बनी रहती है।

questions.text: वैश्वीकरण के किन्हीं चार परिणामों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Explain any four consequences of Globalisation.

key_points: Economic integration — increased flow of goods, services, capital, and labour across borders.
Cultural homogenisation — spread of a uniform global culture, often dominated by Western values.
Erosion of state sovereignty — MNCs and international institutions reduce state autonomy.
Increased inequality — benefits of globalisation are unevenly distributed.
Technological advancement and spread of information technology.

questions.solution: Globalisation has produced far-reaching consequences across economic, political, social, and cultural dimensions. First, economically, globalisation has led to greater integration of national economies through the free flow of goods, services, capital, and labour. Multinational corporations have expanded into developing countries, creating employment but also challenging local industries. Second, politically, globalisation has eroded the absolute sovereignty of nation-states. International organisations like the WTO, IMF, and World Bank exercise considerable influence over national economic policies, limiting state autonomy in decision-making. Third, culturally, globalisation has promoted the spread of a largely Western-dominated global culture through media, entertainment, and consumerism, which threatens the survival of local languages, traditions, and indigenous cultures — a process sometimes described as cultural homogenisation. Fourth, socially, globalisation has intensified inequality both within and between countries. While it has lifted millions out of poverty in some regions, it has also concentrated wealth among a small elite and led to the displacement of workers in sectors unable to compete with cheap imports, deepening social disparities.
questions.solution_hindi: वैश्वीकरण के चार प्रमुख परिणाम निम्नलिखित हैं। प्रथम, आर्थिक दृष्टि से वैश्वीकरण ने वस्तुओं, सेवाओं, पूंजी और श्रम के मुक्त प्रवाह से राष्ट्रीय अर्थव्यवस्थाओं का एकीकरण किया है। द्वितीय, राजनीतिक दृष्टि से इसने राष्ट्र-राज्यों की संप्रभुता को कमजोर किया है। WTO और IMF जैसी संस्थाएं राष्ट्रीय नीतियों को प्रभावित करती हैं। तृतीय, सांस्कृतिक दृष्टि से पश्चिमी संस्कृति के प्रसार से स्थानीय संस्कृतियाँ और परंपराएँ खतरे में पड़ गई हैं। चतुर्थ, सामाजिक दृष्टि से यह असमानता को बढ़ाता है क्योंकि इसके लाभ समान रूप से वितरित नहीं होते।

sub_questions.text_english: "After the disintegration of Soviet Union, India has maintained good relations with all the new independent countries, but the most cordial relations are still there between Russia and India." Justify the statement with two examples.

key_points: Defence cooperation — Russia is India's largest arms supplier.
The Indo-Russian Strategic Partnership signed in 2000.
Cooperation in space technology — ISRO and Russia's space agency.
Energy cooperation — investment in oil fields.
India and Russia share similar positions on multilateral issues like UN reform.

sub_questions.solution: Even after the disintegration of the Soviet Union in 1991, India maintained warm ties with the successor states, but Russia-India relations remained the most cordial. Two examples justify this. First, defence cooperation between India and Russia has been deep and longstanding. Russia continues to be India's largest supplier of military equipment, including fighter aircraft like the Sukhoi-30, aircraft carriers like INS Vikramaditya, nuclear submarines, and missile systems. The BrahMos missile is a joint venture between India and Russia. Second, the two countries signed a Strategic Partnership Agreement in 2000, which was later upgraded to a Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership. This covers cooperation in space technology, energy, trade, and multilateral diplomacy. Both countries have consistently supported each other in multilateral forums like the UN and BRICS on issues of global concern.

sub_questions.text_english: During Cold War period the US economy was more developed than the rest of the world. Still the Soviet system had some special features which distinguish it from the US. Evaluate any two such features.

key_points: The Soviet state owned all means of production — no private property in the capitalist sense.
The Soviet system guaranteed basic needs — employment, healthcare, education — to all citizens.
There was no unemployment in the USSR; the state provided jobs for all.
The Soviet economy was planned and centrally directed, unlike the US free market system.

sub_questions.solution: Although the US economy was materially more developed than the Soviet Union during the Cold War, the Soviet system possessed two distinctive features that set it apart. First, the Soviet system was based on state ownership of the means of production. Unlike the US capitalist model where private individuals and corporations owned factories, land, and businesses, in the USSR everything was owned by the state. This socialist model aimed to eliminate exploitation and ensure that the surplus generated was used for collective welfare rather than individual profit. Second, the Soviet system guaranteed certain basic minimum needs to all its citizens irrespective of their economic status. Every Soviet citizen had guaranteed employment, free healthcare, free education at all levels, and heavily subsidised housing. This social security net was far more comprehensive than what the US offered its citizens, ensuring a basic quality of life for all, even if consumer goods were scarcer than in the West.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain any two main challenges faced by Pakistan in establishing a successful democracy.

key_points: Repeated military coups have destabilised democratic governments.
The military, civil bureaucracy, and feudal landlords dominate politics at the expense of elected representatives.
Religious extremism and sectarian violence undermine civil society and democratic norms.
Pakistan's dependence on US aid has allowed external interference in internal politics.

sub_questions.solution: Pakistan has faced two major challenges in establishing a successful democracy. First, the military has repeatedly intervened in politics, overthrowing elected governments through coups. Since independence, Pakistan has experienced prolonged periods of military rule under leaders like Ayub Khan, Yahya Khan, Zia ul-Haq, and Pervez Musharraf. The military, in alliance with the bureaucracy and feudal elite, has consistently dominated the political system, preventing civilian governments from consolidating democratic institutions and norms. Second, religious extremism and the influence of radical Islamist groups have severely undermined Pakistan's democratic fabric. The rise of the Taliban, sectarian violence, and the use of religion in politics has weakened civil society, suppressed minority rights, and created an environment hostile to liberal democratic values. These factors, combined with Pakistan's complex relationship with militant organisations, have made it extremely difficult to establish a stable and genuinely democratic government.

sub_questions.text_english: "SAARC has taken a major regional initiative in South Asian States to evolve co-operation through multilateral means." Justify the statement with two examples.

SAARC Social Charter addresses social development issues collectively.
SAARC Visa Exemption Scheme facilitates movement of people.

sub_questions.solution: SAARC, founded in 1985, has taken significant regional initiatives to promote cooperation among South Asian nations through multilateral means. Two examples demonstrate this. First, SAARC established the South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA) in 2006, which aimed at reducing tariffs and promoting intra-regional trade among member countries. This was a major multilateral economic initiative to integrate the economies of the region and reduce trade barriers, benefit all member states, and improve the standard of living of South Asian peoples. Second, the SAARC Social Charter, signed in 2004, was a collective commitment by member states to address social development challenges such as poverty alleviation, literacy, health, population stabilisation, women empowerment, and youth development. These multilateral agreements reflect SAARC's role as a platform for cooperative regional governance beyond bilateral relations.

questions.text_english: Describe any four circumstances that led to protests against the Congress Government during 1974-1975.

key_points: Widespread price rise and inflation creating hardship for common people.
Food scarcity and shortage of essential commodities.
Unemployment and economic distress of youth.
Alleged corruption in the Congress government.
The Bihar Movement led by Jayaprakash Narayan demanding Total Revolution.
Railway strike of 1974.

questions.solution: Several circumstances combined to fuel massive protests against the Congress government during 1974-1975. First, the period witnessed steep inflation and a sharp rise in prices of essential commodities like food grains and cooking oil, causing acute hardship to the middle and lower classes. This economic distress sparked popular anger across the country. Second, food scarcity arising from poor agricultural performance and supply disruptions created widespread public frustration, particularly in states like Bihar and Gujarat. Third, growing unemployment, especially among educated youth, created a restive generation that was receptive to calls for political change. Fourth, widespread allegations of corruption within the Congress government and its administration eroded public trust. These factors were channelled into organised political movements: the Gujarat Navnirman Andolan in 1974 and the Bihar Movement led by veteran socialist Jayaprakash Narayan, who called for a Total Revolution to transform the political, social, and economic system, ultimately setting the stage for the Emergency of 1975.

questions.text_english: Describe the events that took place in Sikkim from the time of India's independence to its merger with India.

key_points: Sikkim was a protectorate of India after independence, not a fully sovereign state.
India was responsible for Sikkim's defence, external affairs and communications.
The Chogyal (king) ruled Sikkim and wanted to maintain independence.
A pro-democracy movement grew in Sikkim demanding merger with India.
A referendum was held in 1975, and the people voted overwhelmingly for merger.
Sikkim formally became the 22nd state of India in April 1975.

questions.solution: After India's independence in 1947, Sikkim did not merge with India like other princely states. Instead, it became a protectorate of India in 1950, under which India controlled Sikkim's defence, external affairs, and communications, while the Chogyal (the hereditary ruler) retained internal administration. The Chogyal wished to preserve Sikkim's distinct status and resisted merger with India. However, a strong pro-democracy movement grew among the Sikkimese people, who demanded elections, democratic representation, and eventual merger with India. This movement challenged the Chogyal's authority. In April 1975, the Sikkim Assembly passed a resolution requesting merger with India. Subsequently, a referendum was held in which an overwhelming majority of Sikkimese people voted in favour of merger. Accordingly, the Indian Parliament amended the Constitution to admit Sikkim as the 22nd state of the Indian Union in April 1975, completing its formal integration with India.

The partition of British India in 1947 was based on the two-nation theory and the principle of religious majorities — territories with a Muslim majority went to Pakistan and those with a Hindu majority remained in India. (a) Explain any three reasons for spending more on traditional security than on non-traditional security by India.

sub_questions.text: भारत द्वारा गैर-पारंपरिक सुरक्षा की बजाय पारंपरिक सुरक्षा पर अधिक खर्च करने के किन्हीं तीन कारणों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain any three reasons for spending more on traditional security than on non-traditional security by India.

key_points: Hostile neighbours — Pakistan and China pose military threats requiring strong conventional defence.
Unresolved border disputes with China (Aksai Chin, Arunachal Pradesh) and Pakistan (Kashmir).
Nuclear threats from Pakistan necessitate maintaining a credible nuclear deterrent.
Insurgency in border states requires military presence.
Historical experience of wars (1962, 1965, 1971, 1999) justifies high defence spending.

sub_questions.solution: India allocates more resources to traditional security than to non-traditional security for three primary reasons. First, India faces serious military threats from its immediate neighbours. Both Pakistan and China maintain large, well-equipped armed forces and have engaged India in wars or serious military standoffs. Pakistan's support for cross-border terrorism in Kashmir and China's aggression along the Line of Actual Control (as seen in the 2020 Galwan clash) require India to maintain a powerful conventional military deterrent. Second, India has unresolved territorial disputes with both neighbours. China claims Arunachal Pradesh and occupies Aksai Chin, while Pakistan disputes Indian control over Jammu and Kashmir. These live disputes mean India must keep substantial forces deployed along its borders continuously, requiring large defence budgets. Third, both China and Pakistan are nuclear-armed states. India's doctrine of credible minimum deterrence requires it to maintain a sophisticated nuclear arsenal and the delivery systems (ballistic missiles, nuclear submarines) to make its deterrent credible, all of which demand enormous financial investment. These factors together explain why traditional security spending dominates India's defence budget.

sub_questions.text: सुरक्षा के लिए खतरे के किन्हीं तीन नये स्रोतों की उदाहरण सहित व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain any three new sources of threat to security with examples.

key_points: Terrorism — Al-Qaeda, ISIS attacks threaten both state and human security.
Drug trafficking — international narcotics trade funds criminal and terrorist networks.
Global pandemics — COVID-19 demonstrated how diseases can threaten national and global security.
Climate change and environmental degradation threaten food, water, and human security.
Human trafficking and illegal migration.

sub_questions.solution: The concept of security has expanded beyond military threats to include several new non-traditional sources of danger. Three significant new sources of threat to security are as follows. First, international terrorism has emerged as one of the most serious threats to both national and human security. Terrorist organisations like Al-Qaeda and ISIS operate across national borders, recruit members globally, and carry out devastating attacks on civilian populations, as seen in the 9/11 attacks on the United States (2001) and the 26/11 Mumbai attacks (2008). Terrorism challenges state authority, creates fear among populations, and forces governments to divert enormous resources to counter-terrorism. Second, global pandemics represent a growing non-traditional security threat. The COVID-19 pandemic (2019-2022) demonstrated how a rapidly spreading infectious disease can collapse healthcare systems, devastate economies, kill millions, and destabilise governments — threatening human security on a scale comparable to a major war. Third, climate change and environmental degradation pose existential threats to human security. Rising sea levels threaten to submerge island nations like the Maldives. Desertification and water scarcity in regions like sub-Saharan Africa are causing food insecurity, large-scale migration, and conflict over resources. These challenges cannot be addressed by military means alone and require multilateral cooperation.

sub_questions.text_english: While the Chinese economy has improved dramatically, why has everyone in China not received the benefits of the reforms ? State any three reasons.

key_points: Unemployment has risen as state-owned enterprises were restructured and workers laid off.
Rural-urban inequality has grown — coastal cities prospered while interior rural areas remained poor.
The dismantling of the 'iron rice bowl' — social security guarantees of food, healthcare, and employment were reduced.
Environmental degradation harmed the livelihoods of many communities.
Workers' rights are restricted — no independent trade unions, making it hard to negotiate for wages.

sub_questions.solution: Despite China's remarkable economic growth since the 1978 reforms, the benefits have not been shared equally by all sections of society for three key reasons. First, the economic reforms involved the dismantling of the old socialist 'iron rice bowl' system under which the state guaranteed employment, food, healthcare, and housing to all workers. As state-owned enterprises were privatised or restructured, millions of workers were retrenched and lost their guaranteed social security benefits, pushing many into poverty or insecurity rather than prosperity. Second, economic growth has been highly unequal geographically. The coastal regions and Special Economic Zones like Shenzhen, Shanghai, and Guangzhou experienced explosive growth, while the vast interior rural areas — where hundreds of millions of farmers live — saw much slower development. This has created a profound urban-rural and coastal-interior divide, with the rural poor migrating to cities as cheap labour and living in difficult conditions. Third, China's rapid industrialisation has caused severe environmental degradation — air pollution, water contamination, and soil degradation — which has severely harmed the health and livelihoods of communities living near industrial zones, particularly in coal-mining regions and industrial belts, denying them the full benefits of economic growth.

sub_questions.text_english: Describe the process of evolution of the European Union from an Economic Union to an increasingly Political one.

key_points: 1948 — Organisation for European Economic Cooperation (OEEC) established for economic recovery.
1957 — Treaty of Rome created the European Economic Community (EEC).
1992 — Maastricht Treaty transformed the EEC into the European Union, expanding its scope to political cooperation.
Introduction of a common currency (Euro) in 1999.
Establishment of European Parliament with elected members.
Common foreign and security policy developed.
EU now has its own flag, anthem, and passport.

sub_questions.solution: The European Union's evolution from a primarily economic arrangement to an increasingly political organisation is a gradual, decades-long process. In the aftermath of World War II, European leaders recognised that economic integration was essential to prevent another devastating conflict. In 1948, the Organisation for European Economic Cooperation (OEEC) was established to manage post-war Marshall Plan aid and coordinate economic recovery. This was followed by the Treaty of Paris in 1951, which created the European Coal and Steel Community (ECSC) integrating the coal and steel industries of France, West Germany, Italy, Belgium, Netherlands, and Luxembourg. In 1957, the Treaty of Rome established the European Economic Community (EEC), creating a common market with free movement of goods, capital, and labour. This was the cornerstone of economic integration. The decisive shift toward political integration came with the Maastricht Treaty of 1992, which transformed the EEC into the European Union. This treaty introduced the concept of European citizenship, launched the process toward a common currency (the Euro, adopted in 1999), and created a framework for a Common Foreign and Security Policy. The European Parliament, directly elected by EU citizens, gave the EU a democratic political character. Over time, the EU developed its own flag, anthem, court of justice, and diplomatic service, making it an increasingly political entity that acts collectively on global issues.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain any three major developments which took place in Indian politics during the last decade of the 20th century.

key_points: The rise of coalition politics and end of Congress dominance at the national level.
The rise of the BJP as a major national party (1991-1999).
Economic liberalisation (1991) and its political implications.
Demolition of Babri Masjid (1992) and rise of communal politics.
The Mandal Commission controversy and rise of OBC politics.
The Kargil War (1999).

sub_questions.solution: The last decade of the 20th century (1990-2000) witnessed three major developments that transformed Indian politics. First, this decade marked the decisive end of Congress dominance at the national level and the rise of coalition governments. After the 1989 elections, no single party was able to secure an absolute majority in the Lok Sabha, ushering in an era of coalition politics. Multiple unstable coalition governments — the Janata Dal government of V.P. Singh, the Chandrashekhar government, the United Front governments — characterised the decade, until the BJP-led NDA government under Atal Bihari Vajpayee achieved a stable majority in 1999. Second, the Mandal Commission controversy of 1990 transformed Indian electoral politics by mobilising Other Backward Classes (OBCs) as a decisive political force. When V.P. Singh's government announced the implementation of the Mandal Commission recommendations for 27% reservation for OBCs in government jobs, it triggered massive protests and counter-protests, and permanently altered caste-based political mobilisation across India, empowering parties like Samajwadi Party, RJD, and JD(U). Third, India's economic liberalisation in 1991, initiated by Prime Minister Narasimha Rao and Finance Minister Manmohan Singh, fundamentally changed the direction of Indian economic policy from socialism toward a market economy. This also generated new political debates about globalisation, inequality, and the role of the state, reshaping the agenda of Indian politics for decades.

sub_questions.text: 1989 के बाद गहन प्रतिस्पर्धा और कई संघर्षों के बीच, अधिकांश दलों में उभरी आम सहमति के किन्हीं तीन बिंदुओं को स्पष्ट कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: In the midst of severe competition and many conflicts after 1989, a consensus appeared to have emerged among most parties. Explain any three points of consensus.

key_points: Acceptance of new economic policies — liberalisation, privatisation, and globalisation.
Acceptance of the importance of federalism and the role of states.
Agreement on the necessity of accommodating social justice concerns — OBC reservations, Dalit welfare.
Broad acceptance of the foreign policy direction including improved relations with the US.
Consensus on the need for political stability through coalition management.

sub_questions.solution: Despite fierce competition among political parties after 1989, a broad consensus emerged on three important issues. First, virtually all major political parties came to accept the new economic policies of liberalisation, privatisation, and globalisation. Even parties that had historically supported socialist economics moderated their opposition to market-oriented reforms, recognising that economic growth through liberalisation was necessary. While there were differences in emphasis and speed, no major party proposed reversing liberalisation. Second, there emerged a broad consensus on the importance of social justice and the need to provide representation and welfare to historically marginalised communities. The implementation of the Mandal Commission's OBC reservations and subsequent expansions of affirmative action policies found wide acceptance across the political spectrum, as parties across ideologies competed to champion the cause of backward classes, Dalits, and tribals. Third, most parties developed a consensus on maintaining political stability through coalition management and respecting the federal character of the Indian state. State governments and regional parties gained greater political importance, and central governments — regardless of their political colour — came to recognise the necessity of consulting and accommodating state governments in national decision-making, strengthening cooperative federalism.

sub_questions.text_english: "The foreign policy of independent India has pursued the dream of a peaceful world." Support the statement with any three suitable arguments.

key_points: India adopted Non-Alignment as a foreign policy principle, refusing to join either Cold War bloc.
India co-founded the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) in 1961.
India has consistently participated in UN peacekeeping operations.
India has advocated for nuclear disarmament and signed the CTBT (though not NPT).
India maintained Panchsheel (Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence) as a guide to bilateral relations.

sub_questions.solution: Independent India's foreign policy has consistently pursued peace through three major approaches. First, India adopted the policy of Non-Alignment as a cornerstone of its foreign policy under Jawaharlal Nehru. At the height of the Cold War, when the world was divided into two armed camps led by the USA and USSR, India refused to join either military bloc. Instead, India, along with Egypt's Nasser and Yugoslavia's Tito, co-founded the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) in 1961, which provided an alternative platform for newly independent nations to pursue an independent foreign policy based on peaceful coexistence, sovereignty, and mutual respect. This was a principled stand for a world free from great-power conflict and arms races. Second, India has been one of the most consistent and active contributors to United Nations peacekeeping operations across the world — in Congo, Korea, Cyprus, Lebanon, Cambodia, and many other conflict zones. By contributing troops, police, and civilian personnel to UN missions, India has demonstrated its commitment to resolving conflicts peacefully and upholding international law and the UN Charter. Third, India has been a persistent advocate of universal nuclear disarmament. India's 1988 Rajiv Gandhi Action Plan presented to the UN called for a comprehensive time-bound programme to eliminate all nuclear weapons from the world. India's doctrine of 'No First Use' of nuclear weapons and its advocacy for a Nuclear Weapons Convention reflect its commitment to a world free of nuclear threats, even as it maintains a minimum deterrent for self-defence.

sub_questions.text: "भारत विऔपनिवेशीकरण की प्रक्रिया का एक प्रबल समर्थक और रंगभेद की नीति का कट्टर विरोधी रहा है।" इस कथन के पक्ष में कोई तीन उपयुक्त तर्क दीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: "India was a staunch supporter of the decolonization process and firmly opposed racism." Support the statement with any three suitable arguments.

key_points: India supported African and Asian independence movements through the UN and NAM.
India was the first country to impose trade sanctions on apartheid South Africa.
India consistently raised the issue of apartheid at the UN and international forums.
India extended diplomatic and moral support to the African National Congress (ANC).
India's own freedom struggle under Gandhi inspired anti-colonial movements worldwide.

sub_questions.solution: India's support for decolonisation and opposition to racism is demonstrated by three compelling arguments. First, India was among the first nations to champion the cause of decolonisation at the United Nations. Having itself won freedom from British colonial rule in 1947 after a long and painful struggle, India's leaders understood the aspirations of colonised peoples across Asia and Africa. India used its voice in the UN General Assembly consistently to support the right to self-determination and independence of colonial territories. India played an active role in the Asian-African Conference at Bandung (1955), which became a platform for solidarity among newly independent nations opposing colonialism. Second, India was the very first country in the world to break off diplomatic relations and impose trade sanctions against South Africa to protest the inhuman apartheid policy of racial segregation enforced by the white minority government there. India's action in 1946 — raising the issue of the treatment of Indians in South Africa in the UN — was the first time a racial discrimination issue was taken up in the UN. India maintained this principled opposition to apartheid for over four decades until Nelson Mandela was released and apartheid was dismantled. Third, India provided diplomatic support, moral encouragement, and solidarity to liberation movements across Southern Africa — including the African National Congress (ANC) in South Africa, SWAPO in Namibia, and the MPLA in Angola — giving their leaders a platform and recognition on the world stage, which helped sustain the international pressure that ultimately ended colonial rule in Africa.
